newsitem.title: CHINA: China to boost control over data gathering.
newsitem.headline: China to boost control over data gathering.

text.p: China will tighten supervision of its statistics gatherers to ensure against fraud and the leakage of state secrets, the People's Daily Overseas Edition said on Tuesday.

The State Statistical Bureau, the Ministry of Supervision and the Bureau of Legislative Affairs of the State Council would jointly inspect the gathering and dissemination of statistics by government and non-government agencies, the newspaper said.
It also said the inspection would be designed to ensure that data conformed with the revision of the statistics law approved last year.
That revision included provisions aimed at eliminating deliberately inaccurate data as well as protecting confidential commercial information of domestic enterprises.
The newspaper quoted the bureau's newly installed director Liu Hong as saying the leaking of state secrets had resulted in serious commercial losses to the state. He did not elaborate.
The newspaper also said inspections would cover household surveys and would be applied to foreign organisations.

An official at the State Statistical Bureau told Reuters that certain opinion polls on "sensitive" issues such as political questions were not acceptable, and that the gathering of statistics on household income and spending levels could also be defined as objectionable.
Surveys that benefited investment or development were acceptable, he said.
It was unclear how the regulations would be enforced.
Many foreign survey companies gather market and other statistical data on China.
